Full dataset: linear projections (PCA and ICA) · variant textonly

A one-off companion to the book-only PCA/ICA report, now for all 2,528 chunks: 956 from articles, 592 from the books, 980 from videos, each embedded from its own text only. PCA and ICA are linear: every axis is one fixed direction in the 1,024-dimensional embedding space, so the axes can be read. Unlike the books, most chunks have no chapter, so each axis is described by the chunks at its ends, the video tags and book chapters that are over-represented there, and how much of it is explained by the source.

What was done

  1. Centring. The average vector of all chunks was subtracted (no per-source correction: the source effect is part of what this report measures).
  2. PCA finds the directions of largest variation, in order (PC1 the largest).
  3. ICA (FastICA, 20 components) finds directions whose scores are as independent and long-tailed as possible; each tends to pick out one theme or one kind of text. Signs were set so the long tail is positive.
  4. Describing an axis. For the 30 chunks scoring highest (and for PCA also lowest): their mix of sources, the video tags most over-represented among them compared with all videos (shown if at least 3 of the videos carry the tag), the book chapters they come from, and the first titles.
  5. Source effect. η² (eta squared) = share of an axis' variance explained by the source alone, from 0 (none) to 1 (the axis only tells articles, books and videos apart).

PCA: how much does each direction explain?

Reading it: PC1 explains 6.6%, PC2 3.3%; the first 20 components explain 33%, and 50 are needed for half. PC1 stands out more than in the books alone, and the table below shows why: it is largely the kind of text.

Reading it: PC1 has a source η² of 0.39: it mostly separates book prose (low end) from video descriptions (high end); average PC1 scores: articles -0.03, books -0.17, videos +0.13. This is the source clustering found in the UMAP reports, appearing as the single strongest linear direction. The further components are mostly topical (small η²): capitalism and anarchist theory against practical life, crypto against self-governance, and so on.

Reading it: 10 components are themes that run across articles, books and videos: IC1: Litecoin, Monero; IC2: rakouská ekonomická škola; IC3: kampaň na Startovači, Startovač; IC4: alkohol, MDMA; IC5: vlastnická práva, princip neagrese; IC6: vzdělávání, školství; IC7: 4D, rakouská ekonomická škola; IC8: 22. Láska; IC9: kapitalismus; IC10: zdravotní pojištění, zdravotnictví. They are the linear counterpart of the topic regions on the maps, and they connect the same subject across sources. 10 components describe a kind of text rather than a subject: IC11: Vypnutí prázdninového módu 2020 (articles); IC12: Gabriela a Urza s láskou ke svobodě a učení ( (articles); IC13: Gabriela, Urza, Jotka, Amálka a Verča s lásko (videos); IC14: Crowdfunding (videos); IC15: Tereza v deCentrále: Právo žít, právo umírat (articles); IC16: Příběh druhý (books); IC17: Pavel Ševčík: Kulturní válka v Hollywoodu a j (videos); IC18: Ministerstvo dopravy versus vodáci (articles); IC19: Anarchokapitalismus v prvej línii: Monopoly (videos); IC20: Urza a Tim debatují s Gabrielou Svárovskou a (videos). Most are recurring formats (announcements, yearly notices, a video series, conference recordings) whose texts are alike because of their template. A few may instead be subjects that only one source covers (check their top texts): that is itself a coverage finding, not a defect.

Reading it: lower is more mixed. A map built on the two focused ICA themes mixes sources far more than PC1 × PC2, because it leaves out the source direction that dominates PC1.

Conclusions

  • The strongest linear direction is the kind of text. PC1 separates book prose from video descriptions (η² 0.39), confirming in linear form what the UMAP reports found: style and length are a large part of the embedding.
  • Beneath it, the directions are topical. From PC2 on, and in most ICA components, the source explains little; the axes are subjects.
  • ICA separates themes from formats. 10 of 20 components are cross-source themes, 10 are formats or series. The theme components show where Urza addresses the same idea in books, articles and videos; the format components identify template texts (announcements, notices, series intros) that a coverage measure may want to discount.
  • For the coverage map: scoring a political question along the theme components would show which of Urza's themes it touches; the format components are a tool for spotting boilerplate. As in the book report, components depend on the number chosen and the random start: a lens, not a fixed taxonomy.
